appendix_a: **Data:** only the two IRCC CSV files [1, 2], in the IRCC open data release of September 15, 2026 (data to July 2026) (files retrieved October 16, 2026), read with the Temporary Workers dashboard code [13], which shows the same release, so every IRCC number matches the dashboard. Latest month: July 2026. Background sources are cited for context only; the one outside number is Statistics Canada's estimate of the fall in non-permanent residents [12], a count of people, not permits.

**Measure:** a flow. Each value counts work permits issued in a month, as the dashboard calls them (IRCC's wording is "became effective": the month the permit was signed and given to the person), by intended province or territory. New permits, renewals and changes of status all count. Annual figures are sums of months, labelled "permits", not people, and are not the number of workers present on a date.
**Part-year:** 2026 covers January to July and is only compared with January to July of earlier years.

**Rounding in the note:** the body rounds counts to the nearest thousand (or to two decimals of a million) and percentages to whole numbers. Appendix D lists every rounded number with its exact value and where to find it.

**Suppression:** cells shown as "--" (0 to 5) are counted as 0, so totals may be slightly understated (at most 5 per suppressed cell: under 1% for TFWP and about 2% for IMP over the period, computed from the two CSVs). Other values are rounded to 5 by IRCC; sums are of rounded values.

**Canada** = the 13 provinces and territories plus "province/territory not stated" (the files have no Canada row). "Not stated" counts in Canada but is never ranked, so provincial shares add to slightly under 100%.

**TFWP and IMP do not overlap**, so "both programs" = TFWP + IMP. IRCC's IMP table covers only a subset of IMP permit holders: it leaves out people in Canada mainly for other reasons, such as asylum claimants.

**Figures** are pictures of the Temporary Workers dashboard's own charts [13] (plain-language version, October 19, 2026), with its card titles and source lines, taken from the dashboard in its default setting (the release above). The caption under each states its takeaway and names the tab; the filters are: Figure 1 (Overview tab): Canada, both programs, Annual view, show only Jan–Jul of each year, Jan 2015 to Jul 2026; Figure 2 (Geography tab): British Columbia (highlighted), both programs, period ending July 2026. Some numbers have no chart in the dashboard (Unknown IMP as a share of all permits and of Alberta's increase, permits other than PGWPs in Table 1, and the robustness check below); they are calculated from the same two IRCC files (Appendix D). Figure 1's axis labels each bar "(Jan–Jul)", as the dashboard does when only January–July is shown.

**Streams** are grouped from IRCC's program levels as in the dashboard (mapping in the dashboard's About the data tab; IRCC's own program names per group are on the Composition tab). "Non-farm (employer-sponsored) permits" = IRCC's "Other Temporary Foreign Workers with LMIA" (dashboard: "Other TFWP workers with an LMIA"). "Farm permits" = the Seasonal Agricultural Worker Program plus other agricultural workers. "Unknown IMP" (IRCC does not identify the program; dashboard: "Unknown or other IMP") is kept separate; in this release it is entirely IRCC's "Unknown" program, as its other codes are suppressed cells counted as 0.

**Robustness check:** leaving permits with no province or territory stated out of Canada (so Canada = the 13 provinces and territories), B.C. supplied {bc_contrib_ytd_pt} of the January–July 2026 increase, against its {bc_share_ytd25_pt} share of permits a year earlier ({bc_contrib_ytd} and {bc_share_ytd25} with them included), so the finding on B.C.'s share does not depend on that group.

**One time frame:** the body compares January–July 2026 with January–July of earlier years (and full calendar years up to 2025); "highest January–July in the data" means above January–July of every year from 2015 to 2025.
**Share of the increase** = a province's change in permits divided by Canada's change over the same months, as in the dashboard's chart of each province's share of Canada's change (Figure 2).

**Permits vs. people:** permit counts are a flow and are never used as a count of temporary workers in Canada. Statistics Canada's non-permanent resident estimates [12] count people living in Canada on a date, so the two can move in opposite directions, as they do in 2025–2026.

**Unknown IMP check:** if PGWPs had only moved out of "Unknown IMP", that group would have fallen in 2026; it rose (checked in analysis_q2.R). Identified streams are still a lower bound for each stream, because some Unknown IMP permits may belong to any stream.
**Percentages** are recalculated from the raw counts and rounded once, from the exact value (B.C.'s +30.46% is shown as 30%); the appendix tables and Appendix D show them to one decimal.

**Policy events** are dated context from official sources (Appendix B). The cohort explanation for the 2026 PGWP rise is labelled as untested, and the explanation for permits rising while people fall (new PGWPs go to graduates already in Canada [11]) as likely.
**Reader:** a ministry manager or executive who is not a data specialist; jargon is defined on first use.
appendix_e: analysis_q2.R opens the dashboard's data (IRCC open data release of September 15, 2026 (data to July 2026): the two CSV files, saved in ../q1/data/baseline.rds; no live download) with the dashboard's code (../q1/R/data.R, ../q1/R/calc.R), computes every number, and writes facts_q2.csv and the tables.

dashboard/Mohsen_2_dashboard_shots.R starts an unchanged copy of the dashboard (commit 7d2fad4) in a headless browser, sets the filters named under each figure and saves the dashboard card as a picture (tables/figure_register.csv lists each figure's card title and filters).

word/build_r2_docx.py builds this Word document (Mohsen_2.docx) from Mohsen's text (word/mohsen_text.md, used verbatim); tables/body_numbers.csv links each rounded number in it to facts_q2.csv. LibreOffice converts the document to Mohsen_2.pdf.

validate_q2.R recomputes every count from the IRCC data with independent base-R code, recalculates every percentage from its counts, checks that every number in the body is the rounded value of its fact, checks headline figures against the dashboard functions, and checks the word count, page count, citations, links and the Word file.
Every script installs any missing R packages first. The Temporary Workers dashboard: https://mohsenfazeli.shinyapps.io/temporary-workers-dashboard/
AI use is described in the AI Disclosure Statement (Mohsen_AI.docx).
